newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian columnist detained, his paper says.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian columnist detained, his paper says.

text.p: Nigeria's independent Vanguard newspaper said on Tuesday Nigerian security men arrested one of its political columnists last week.

"Dele Sobowale, who was picked up from Vanguard premises last weekend has since been held incommunicado and denied access by employers and members of his family," the paper said in a front-page report.
It did not say why he was detained and Nigerian security agencies do not usually comment on such detentions.

The Vanguard, like most Lagos-based newspapers, is critical of the military government in Nigeria which has been in turmoil over annulment of a presidential poll in 1993 that would have restored democracy.
Sobowale writes a weekly column in which he has criticised a new programme to restore democracy next year.
He is the second journalist to be held since December. Godwin Agbroko, editor of Theweek magazine, has been detained since last month and no reason has been given for the detention.

Human rights groups have condemned the latest arrest, saying the government should be more tolerant of press criticisms in the run-up to 1998 when it has promised to hand over to a democratically elected president.
"There should be an unfettered flow of information since we are transiting to democracy," said Abdul Oroh, executive director of the Civil Liberties Organisation in a statement.
